title: I built a 33-factor ticker research tool and made its evidence visible
author: ExplanationNormal339
selftext:
Disclosure: I build AimyTrade. I am looking for feedback from people who actually use algorithmic stock research.

A score can look precise while hiding weak inputs. I wanted a ticker read where the price/technical, institutional, insider/social, and news/catalyst evidence is visible alongside the calculated invalidation levels. The output is algorithmic and non-personalized; it can be wrong. The scorecard and calibration are public so the result is open to scrutiny.

Here is a live INTC example: https://aimytrade.io/ticker/intc?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=ai_trading_evidence_sep25

One full ticker read is free. For regular use, Starter is $9/month for 30 analyses and 10 active thesis monitors. Pro is $29/month for unlimited analyses and 50 monitors. No false countdown or performance guarantee.

If you use this kind of tool, what would make the read credible to you: transparent inputs, historical calibration, a clearly stated invalidation condition, or something else? I can answer specific questions here.

Educational analytics only. This is not personalized investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold a security. Research independently and consult a licensed financial advisor.

comments.author: ExplanationNormal339
comments.body: Founder follow-up for anyone comparing the paid option after the free INTC example: [Starter is $9/month](https://aimytrade.io/pricing?plan=starter&utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=comment&utm_campaign=ai_trading_evidence_sep25) for 30 algorithmic analyses and 10 active thesis monitors. The plan page shows the full terms. I would be interested in specific evidence you would want to inspect before relying on a ticker read; missing inputs and uncertainty should be visible. This is educational, non-personalized analysis, not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: a stated invalidation, and then a public list of every past read with its date and whether it hit. calibration charts are easy to make look good, a plain dated list is a lot harder to fake.

replies.author: ExplanationNormal339
replies.body: A dated, per-read record with the evaluation horizon and outcome criteria fixed when each read is issued would be a stronger audit than an aggregate calibration chart. The current ticker read shows calculated invalidation levels, but I cannot point you to a complete public ledger of every past read, including misses, today. I don't want the chart to imply that level of proof. Thanks for spelling out the standard.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: saying it on the page is the right call. even a short dated list that starts today would count for more than the chart.

replies.author: ExplanationNormal339
replies.body: That is a fair standard. AimyTrade does not yet have a public row-by-row dated history, so I would not treat the calibration chart as proof of individual calls. The useful record should include each ticker, the original timestamped read, a fixed outcome window, and unresolved cases without cherry-picking. I am working on making that public; until then, the gap is real.

replies.author: ExplanationNormal339
replies.body: Correction to my last reply: I overlooked an existing public page, https://aimytrade.io/results . It lists dated, eligible public analyses and their tracked outcomes for the last 30 days. I checked the live data just now. It is a filtered sample, not every past read, so it still does not meet your stronger all-history standard. I should have pointed you to the sample while being clear about that limit.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the dated list with the misses left in is what I'd read first when it's up. most tools in this space never say the gap out loud.

replies.author: ExplanationNormal339
replies.body: You're looking for the full dated ledger, misses included, with the outcome window fixed up front. I build AimyTrade, and I need to correct the link I posted above: /results currently redirects to the home page, so I was wrong to call it a readable public page. The raw 30-day filtered sample is available as JSON at https://aimytrade.io/api/performance/results?range=month ; it includes timestamps and losing rows, but it excludes some analyses and is not a complete record with a fixed outcome horizon for every original read. The all-issued ledger you're asking for is not public yet. I won't present the sample as if it were that ledger.
